title: Introduction to Routing 🌐
description: Learn why SPAs need routing and how the Angular Router transforms your app.

slides.title: The SPA Problem: One Page, Many Views 🤔
slides.content:
# Why Do We Need Routing?

A traditional website navigates by loading entirely new HTML pages. A **Single Page Application (SPA)** loads only one page, then dynamically changes what the user sees.

* Without routing, an SPA can only show one view at a time with no way to bookmark or share a state.
* Routing maps **URL paths** to specific components, making your app feel like a multi‑page site while staying fast.
* Benefits: deep linking, back/forward browser buttons work, better user experience.

quizData.question: What problem does routing solve in a Single Page Application?

options.text: It allows URL‑based navigation between views without full page reloads.

quizData.explanation: Routing maps URLs to components, enabling navigation and deep linking while staying on the same page.

slides.title: Meet the Angular Router 🧭
slides.content:
# The Angular Router

Angular includes a powerful **Router** library (`@angular/router`) that:

* Lets you define an array of **Routes** (URL ↔ component mappings).
* Provides a `<router-outlet>` directive that acts as a placeholder where the routed component renders.
* Handles browser history and URL changes automatically.
* Supports route parameters, guards, child routes, and lazy loading.

It’s essential for any app with more than one screen.

slides.title: The <router-outlet>
slides.content: The router-outlet is where the magic happens. You place it once (usually in AppComponent) and the router swaps components into it based on the URL.

slides.title: Router vs. Manual DOM Manipulation 🔄
slides.content:
Without the router, you’d have to manually show/hide components with `*ngIf` or `[hidden]`. That’s messy and breaks browser navigation.

The router gives you:
* Clean URL structure (`/products/42`).
* History API integration.
* Lazy loading to reduce initial bundle size.
* Route guards for authentication.

It’s the foundation of every professional Angular app.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Use Routing, Even for Small Apps

Even a simple app benefits from routing. It makes the codebase scalable and users expect URLs they can bookmark.
